summary: The prepared base reproduces the original scheduler invariant failure for a 1024-token chunk inside a 1500-token encoder: prepare_encoder_info_extend reports Expected 0, got -476. At the exact candidate commit, the actual PrefillAdder prevents this state by admitting an oversized encoder atomically when the batch is empty and deferring it when earlier admissions consumed the chunk budget. Focused admission and downstream metadata tests pass across chunk sizes, encoder lengths, page sizes, alignment, and decoder-only multimodal behavior. No native source changed.

tests.what_was_measured: Direct reproduction of the original corrupted metadata invariant; AssertionError: Expected 0, got -476.
Candidate admission behavior: six atomic-boundary subcases, deferral after partial budget use, and unchanged decoder-only multimodal chunking.
Downstream encoder/decoder cache-location and token-count coherence for four admitted atomic encoder chunks.
Full focused suites: 36 tests passed and 28 subtests passed.
Loaded source from /job/repo/python/sglang and schedule_policy.py; PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 saw one AMD Instinct MI350X and independently computed 1024-1500=-476 on device.

gpu_execution.evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X was visible through ROCm 7.2; an on-device integer reference confirmed the failing delta -476. Scheduler regression tests themselves use CPU metadata because the defect is device-independent Python admission/bookkeeping logic.

remaining_limitations: No Whisper weights were downloaded and no end-to-end transcription server was launched.
The source report's Intel XPU architecture was unavailable; validation used shared Python scheduler paths on CPU plus one AMD Instinct MI350X environment probe.
The downstream metadata routine still asserts on a manually fabricated mid-encoder chunk; the candidate fixes the actual production admission path so it does not create that invalid state.
No native/FlyDSL source changed, repository-environment.json records native and wheel as null, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
